messages:
Jane Nguyen: Quick preflight — planning to push runtime v2.4.6 to canary (~5% traffic) in ~30m. Can folks run a short profiling sweep (seq_len=512) and share p99, kv-cache hit breakdown, and any tail-stack traces? Need sign-off from perf + oncall.

Omar Khan: Running a 5min replay now on staging. Initial numbers look off vs baseline. Summary (staging replay): p50=32ms, p95=110ms, p99=340ms. Baseline v2.4.5 p99=~210ms. KV cache hit ~72%. GPU SM 78%, mem 65%.

Omar Khan: Command I used:
```
run_bench --model redwood-v1 --seq 512 --qps 200 --duration 300 --replay traffic/0301
```
Summary output: 
```
p50=32ms p95=110ms p99=340ms tokens/s=4200
perf_probe: tail_stack -> aten::matmul, aten::softmax, cudaLaunchKernel (hot)
kv_cache_hits=72% kv_cache_inserts=28%
```

Liam Chen: Are we sure this is runtime kernel selection / scheduling vs traffic shape? Could be batching window + large sequence combos creating heavy kernels. Suggest trying a reduced max_batch_size and tighter batching window in a quick experiment:
```
runtime:
  max_batch_size: 8
  batching_window_ms: 8
```
If that drops p99, we know it's batching backpressure.

Maria Lopez: Hold on the rollout until we get KV-cache trace. Last month's canary showed similar tail when cache invalidations happened during small-scale traffic bursts. Please run a focused trace on kv_cache.* and capture TTL evictions.
Command: `profiler --filters kv_cache.* --duration 120s --out flame_kv.gz`

sre-oncall: FYI — last canary on 2025-08-17 had a partial degradation (link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-20250817). Not a full outage but started as p99 drift at ~7m in. Would prefer conservative hold if perf team wants more time.

Omar Khan: I can run the kv-cache trace and a flamegraph dump in ~10m, and also try a reduced-batch staging run. If tail persists I'll attempt pinning the kernel-selection flag (revert the auto-kernel heuristic) and test. Proposed rollback criteria if canary shows p99 > baseline + 50% for >5m: cancel rollout and pin kernel-selection to v2.4.5 behavior.

Liam Chen: +1 to that rollback criteria. Also add: if error rate or 5xx spike > 0.5% hold immediately.

Maria Lopez: +1 to hold until trace results. Also ask infra to surface KV cache TTL metrics per model shard (we need to see evictions correlated with requests).

Omar Khan: Quick experiment results (staging, reduced batch): p99 dropped to 220ms with max_batch_size=8 and batching_window_ms=8. Tokens/s down ~8%. Flamegraphs attached (uploaded to #eng-runtime artifacts). KV-cache trace shows short-lived spikes of TTL eviction tied to bursty request patterns — likely cache misses triggering heavy ops.

deploy-bot: Canary pipeline scheduled for 1923457100. Manual hold requested by Jane Nguyen — rollout will not start until hold cleared.

sre-oncall: Noted. I'll monitor and will escalate if any infra alerts during the experiment windows.

Jane Nguyen: Decision: HOLD for now. Omar — capture the full flamegraph and attach the trace + a short writeup with suggested mitigations (reduce batching, increase kv-cache size/ttl, or pin kernel heuristic). We'll reconvene in this thread once artifacts are up. Thanks. :+1:

Omar Khan: Will post artifacts in ~15m and tag perf run results.

Liam Chen: Thanks — holding too.

Maria Lopez: Thanks — holding.

deploy-bot: Manual hold confirmed by Jane Nguyen. Canary start canceled until hold released.
